1499.author: yuanzhou75
1499.body: The desktop idea tree had exactly one scale: the one `fit()` computed from the column width. No wheel, no button and no drag changed it, so a drawing wider than the column could only be read by scrolling at whatever size the column imposed — a wide branch could not be shrunk to see its shape, and a hypothesis could not be enlarged to read it. ## What changed - **`apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaTree.tsx`** - **Zoom.** The wheel zooms the drawing, and a small bar adds `−` / percentage / `＋` / `适应宽度`, both sharing one range (0.4–2). The buttons are ordinary buttons with `aria-label` and `title`, the percentage is an ``, and each button is disabled at the end of the range. The wheel listener is native and non-passive: React's wheel handler is passive, so it could not keep the panel behind the tree from scrolling while the drawing zoomed. The scale is computed first and the event only claimed when it can actually move: at either end of the range, or with no vertical delta, the box keeps the gesture and scrolls. - **Pan.** Dragging the background moves the drawing by scrolling it, so nothing — not a zoom step, not a drag, not a resize — moves the reader's view away from what they were reading. The grab cursor appears only when the drawing is actually bigger than the column. A press that lands on a node button, or on the zoom bar, is that control's press and does not start a pan. - **Double click.** On the background: one step in (×1.5), and a second double click back to the column's fit. - **Keyboard.** With the tree focused, `+` / `-` zoom and `0` fits; the region is focusable and shows a focus ring (`aria-keyshortcuts="+ - 0"`). - A scale set by hand survives new nodes arriving and a resize. Before this, `ResizeObserver` re-fitted on every layout change, which is exactly the state a running research is in; a new tree, or the fit control, still starts from the column's own fit. - **`apps/desktop/src/styles/idea-tree.css`** — the tree gets a positioned wrapper (`.idea-tree-shell`) and the bar is its child, absolutely placed at the wrapper's top-right; the grab / grabbing cursors; the focus ring. The bar is **not** inside the scroller. - **`apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/text/en.ts`** — four labels (canvas zoom, zoom in, zoom out, fit width). - **`apps/desktop/tests/idea-tree-view.test.tsx`** — eight cases: the fit never magnifies and stops at the readable floor; the hand range clamps; a wheel asks for a scale and reports when it cannot move the one it has (pixels, lines, pages, both ends, a zero delta); zooming keeps the viewport's middle over the same drawing; an automatic fit leaves a hand-set scale alone; the component's own buttons take 100% → 120% → 144% while a new graph keeps 144%; the keyboard zooms and `0` fits; and a double click zooms one step and then returns to the fit. - **`apps/desktop/tests/idea-tree-legacy.test.tsx`, `apps/desktop/tests/idea-tree-stale-node.test.tsx`** — select a node by `idea-tree-node-button` instead of "the first button", so the new controls are not counted as node buttons. This is the **desktop** implementation. The browser workbench draws its own tree (`apps/web/src/IdeaTreeCanvas.tsx`, whose wheel zoom is reset by each graph update); that is a separate component with its own tests and is not touched here. ## Behaviour, measured Same component, same 360px column, same graph. Real wheel, real drag, real click, real double click and real key presses, read back from the DOM: | | result | |---|---| | wheel, one step | fit **60%** → **75.1%** | | next graph update | still **75.1%** | | `适应宽度` | back to **60%** | | a real click on `＋` | **60% → 72%** | | a real click on `−` | **72% → 60%** | | drag 50px left on the background | `scrollLeft` **78 → 128** | | a drag that starts on the bar | pan did not move (`scrollLeft` unchanged) | | double click on the background | **60% → 90%** (×1.5) | | second double click | **90% → 60%** (the fit) | | `+` with the tree focused | **60% → 72%** | | `0` with the tree focused | **72% → 60%** | | at 149%, scrolled fully right | bar at x **165–322** inside the tree's **12–348** | | at 200%, one wheel notch further in | scale held at **200%**, `scrollTop` **80 → 0** (the box got the gesture) | On `main`, the same wheel leaves the scale at 60% and the bar does not exist: there is no zoom at all, which is what the report was about. ## Screenshots Component-level renders of the real `IdeaTreeView` against the app's own `apps/desktop/src/styles/index.css`, in a 360px column. This is not a recording of the whole app; the Electron window is not automated in this environment. Pinned to the storage commit `3a127cf870606f42384a28526a617a7a8aea35ff` (`shots/desktop-idea-tree-zoom/`), from one run of the current head: ![the four states, zh](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/3a127cf870606f42384a28526a617a7a8aea35ff/shots/desktop-idea-tree-zoom/states-zh.png) ![the four states, en](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/3a127cf870606f42384a28526a617a7a8aea35ff/shots/desktop-idea-tree-zoom/states-en.png) The four panels are: this branch at the column's fit, one wheel step in, after the next graph update, and back at the fit after `适应宽度`. Both languages, because the bar carries visible copy and the two are not the same width. At 149%, panned to the far right — the state that used to carry the controls out of view: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/3a127cf870606f42384a28526a617a7a8aea35ff/shots/desktop-idea-tree-zoom/zoomed-scrolled-zh.png After a drag, the same drawing at the same scale, moved: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/3a127cf870606f42384a28526a617a7a8aea35ff/shots/desktop-idea-tree-zoom/panned-zh.png For comparison, `main` at the same column and the same graph: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yuanzhou75/sciencediscovery/3a127cf870606f42384a28526a617a7a8aea35ff/shots/desktop-idea-tree-zoom/main-zh.png ## Fixes in this head (`9c3fc16a`) - **Clicks on the zoom bar did nothing.** A press on the bar started a pan: `onPointerDown` captured the pointer on the scroller, `pointerup` was retargeted to the scroller, and the browser sent the click there instead of to the button. Now a press inside `.idea-tree-zoom` is left to the bar (as a press on a node already was), and a double click on the bar no longer bubbles into the canvas gesture. Verified with real clicks, not `props.onClick`: see the two click rows above. - **The bar scrolled out of the viewport horizontally.** `position: sticky; top: 0` pins one axis only, and the zoom itself re-centres the drawing. The bar now lives in a non-scrolling wrapper beside the scroller and is positioned against it, so it keeps the tree's corner on both axes — measured at 149% with the drawing scrolled fully right, and in the `zoomed-scrolled-zh` frame. - **The wheel swallowed every gesture.** It now computes the clamped scale first and only claims the event when the scale actually changes; at the 40% / 200% ends, or with no vertical delta, the box scrolls instead of going dead. Measured above at 200%. - **Two existing desktop tests were red** (`idea-tree-legacy.test.tsx:87` counted 5 buttons, `idea-tree-stale-node.test.tsx:49` took the zoom-out button as the node). Both now select `.idea-tree-node-button`, like `idea-tree-view.test.tsx` already did. ## Tests - `apps/desktop/tests/idea-tree-view.test.tsx`, `idea-tree-legacy.test.tsx`, `idea-tree-stale-node.test.tsx`: **21 pass / 0 fail**. The files are tagged `os:linux`; on this Windows host they were run as copies with only the platform tag changed to `os:windows`, deleted afterwards. - The whole `apps/desktop` suite on this host: **163 pass / 0 fail**, 139 skipped because they are tagged `os:linux`; CI runs those on Linux. - `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — clean on the pre-rebase worktree (main `940ea4f0` plus these files). The pushed head is main `a19476ae` plus the same seven files, and CI typechecks that tree; this host cannot install main's workspace packages to repeat the check locally. - Mutation: removing the guard that lets a hand-set scale survive an automatic fit turns that case red. - The frames were taken behind two gates: every `` fully loaded (`complete` and `naturalWidth > 0`) and no request answered 4xx, or the run aborts and writes nothing. The gestures above were exercised with real browser input events, not by writing the state directly. ## Optional notes from the review, not taken - **Zoom about the pointer** (`EvolveTree` does): this zooms about the viewport centre. Centring is what keeps `ideaTreeScrollAfterZoom` a pure ratio of the middle and testable as "the same drawing column under the middle"; pointer-anchored zoom is a different contract and a different gesture for `EvolveTree` to converge on, not something to slot in here. - **Composing the pending scroll across a burst of wheel events**: a flick can still compute each step from the scroll that has not been applied yet. Left as is — the target is overwritten, not composed, and a burst lands within a few pixels. - **`IDEA_TREE_ZOOM_MIN = 0.4` below the fit's readable 0.6**: deliberate, as the review says. The comment on the constant says the hand range is the reader's choice; the fit stays readable. ## Scope Only the tree view. `IdeaNodeDetail`, the research card, the panel and the create dialog are untouched; no product text is removed, and the node list keeps its own controls.
